1The control plane is the scheduler#

CEP runs no Kubernetes and no per-session VMs. A Go control plane drives the Docker Engine API directly on one (later a few) beefy host(s) — it is the scheduler.

invariant

One binary

cep ops provisions boxes, proxies the terminal, serves the si-rendered content, and runs step checks.

invariant

Budget, not count

admission is by a RAM budget, never a container cap.

safe nesting

Nested-Docker box

the student deploys CockroachDB inside their own sandbox; the host Docker socket is never exposed.

Honest read: privileged Docker-in-Docker for the demo; sysbox-runc (unprivileged) before untrusted users. Linux-only host.

2Request & networking flow#

How a learner's browser reaches their private box — one origin, path-routed by the gateway.

3Capacity, cost & the Phase-1 plan#

Measured per session — one DinD box running a nested compose of 1–9 CRDB nodes (multi-region means more nodes in the same box, not more VMs). Data is tiny (~10M small rows, on disk), so RAM tracks node count.

Host (always-on) approx $/mo 1-node 3-node 9-node
e2/n2-highmem-8 · 64 GB (Phase 1) ~$250–300 ~50 ~25 ~16
n2-highmem-16 · 128 GB ~$570 ~110 ~55 ~36

Phase 1: one always-on 64 GB VM, --mem-budget-gb 50 --mem-mb 2048 → 25 sessions, internal via LB + IAP. GKE and scheduled start/stop are out (instant availability is required).

4Phases#

  1. Single host · privileged DinD · internal ≤25 sessions.
  2. Sysbox runtime + bigger VM + 1-node topology per track.
  3. Multi-host placement (MIG); the control plane stays the scheduler.
